industry.why: Overweight, from Neutral, on the row's own written condition ('to B when a source carries a healthcare read with the industry's relative strength holding A or B'), met on both legs for the first time: relative strength A (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; C prior), and Kepler (Donneky, 26-Nov) names Roche top pick on its breast cancer pill and AI-led discovery while DNB Carnegie (26-Nov) reads Elekta's conservative guidance and US share as the opportunity, with the Healthcare Industry Memo (26-Nov) verdicts unchanged; see component 1, Special topics, Topic 3. The 27-Nov-26 regime (risk-off in the open, defensives leading on all five windows) pays large, proven, cash-yielding defensives, and Goldman's AI-adoption thesis (Mark Wilson, 20-Nov) names pharma among the adopters. Two live holdings (CVS Group 1.70%, Elekta 3.98%); 26 Pool stocks. Counter-case: a crowded defensive a month before Morgan Stanley's fade window, with Deutsche Bank positioning at the 64th percentile (13-Nov) and the Industry Memo saying the out-of-favour source is less durable for the largest names. Back to C if relative strength leaves A or B, or if the three-month defensives line falls under +2 points.

sector.why: Neutral, carried. No line specific to distribution; relative strength C (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; D prior); Pool name Apotea. No tilt.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. No source spoke to Ireland this week; Pool names AIB, Kerry, Irish Continental. Moves to B if a second source names Ireland as the fiscal exception.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
